Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that most of the prognostic value of tumor depth in soft tissue sarcomas of the extremity or trunk wall can be explained by the association between tumor size and depth. However, a few more detailed explanations are needed to fully address this question.

Tumor depth is an important factor in soft tissue sarcoma prognosis, as it is associated with increased risk of local recurrence and metastasis. Studies have shown that deeper tumors tend to have higher rates of these adverse outcomes. Nevertheless, the relationship between tumor depth and prognosis can be complex, and other factors such as tumor size, grade, and molecular subtype should also be considered.

Including tumor depth in prognostication is not universally agreed upon, but it may be a useful tool for some patients, particularly those with larger tumors or those who are at high risk of recurrence. For example, studies have suggested that tumors deeper than 3 cm may have a higher risk of local recurrence and metastasis.

In the case of soft tissue sarcoma, most guidelines recommend considering tumor size, grade, and molecular subtype in addition to tumor depth when making prognostic predictions. However, including tumor depth specifically may provide additional insight into the tumor's behavior and potential for adverse outcomes.

It is essential to note that individual patients should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis, taking into account their specific tumor characteristics, clinical presentation, and other factors. Healthcare providers should work together to develop an individualized treatment plan that takes into account all relevant information.

In summary, while including tumor depth in prognostication of soft tissue sarcoma may provide additional insight, it is not a one-size-fits-all approach, and healthcare providers should consider the specific patient's situation when making these predictions.
